clue.text: Hit the golf course wearing these!

definitions.text: Hit the golf course wearing these!

parts.note: to cuff someone is to hit them with an open hand
links is a seaside golf course

explanation.surface: A golfer is urged to wear smart shirt accessories while playing a round.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both wordplay and definition: these are what you wear at the cuffs, and the clue joins a blow to a type of golf course.
explanation.definitionFit: Shirt fasteners that join the two sides of a double cuff are worn at the wrist, as the exclamation suggests.

clue.text: Cleaner aims to develop personal quality

parts.note: a char or charwoman is a British cleaning lady

indicators.note: letters that develop grow into a new shape, so the word aims is rearranged

explanation.surface: A cleaning lady sets out to cultivate her own winning traits.
explanation.walkthrough: A CHAR is an old British word for a cleaner; 'to develop' turns AIMS into ISMA.
explanation.definitionFit: Charm or magnetism that draws others is a quality belonging to a person.

clue.text: Almost 50 — accepting one line, but getting cosmetic surgery

indicators.note: accepting means taking something inside, so one piece goes within the other
almost means the last letter of the word for fifty is dropped

parts.note: fifty spelt out
an ace is the one in a pack of cards

explanation.surface: Someone nearly fifty takes on one wrinkle and has a nip and tuck done.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Almost' cuts FIFTY to FIFT, and 'accepting' puts ACE and L inside it: F-ACEL-IFT.
explanation.definitionFit: A surgical tightening of facial skin is the classic cosmetic operation.

clue.text: Field study that's dull

parts.note: lea is a poetic word for a meadow
a den is a private room for work or study

explanation.surface: Studying the subject of fields turns out to be boring.
explanation.definitionFit: Leaden means heavy and lifeless, as dull and uninspired things are.

clue.text: Referring to identity, mean to change Lucy's cover

indicators.note: to change the word mean is to rearrange its letters
the cover of a word is its outside, its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A name is mentioned while someone means to alter Lucy's book jacket.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to change' turns MEAN into NAME; 'cover' gives the first and last letters of Lucy's, L and Y.
explanation.definitionFit: The adverb introduces a specification, saying exactly which person or thing is meant.

clue.text: Miss abroad, end of September in Estonia, drunk

indicators.note: drunk means the letters stagger into a new order
the end of a word is its final letter

explanation.surface: A young lady overseas got tipsy in Estonia at the end of September.
explanation.walkthrough: 'end of' gives R from September; 'drunk' rearranges R with ESTONIA.
explanation.definitionFit: The Spanish title for an unmarried woman is the equivalent of the English 'Miss' used abroad.

clue.text: Photo confirms record?

parts.note: a book of photographs serves as proof of past events, and the same word means an LP record

explanation.surface: A snapshot provides evidence of what happened.
explanation.definitionFit: A bound book of pictures keeps a record of events, and a long-playing disc is also called by this name.

clue.text: A constant member of the clergy, that's right

parts.note: C is the scientific symbol for a constant such as the speed of light
a curate is an assistant parish priest

explanation.surface: A steadfast priest is declared to be correct.
explanation.definitionFit: Correct and precise, as an answer that is right is exact.

clue.text: Injury caused by reportedly hot infusions

indicators.note: reportedly means what is heard, so the word for the drinks is said out loud

parts.note: brews are pots of tea or other hot drinks steeped in water

explanation.surface: Someone is hurt by scalding cups of tea, so people say.
explanation.walkthrough: BREWS, spoken, sounds like the injury.
explanation.definitionFit: A discoloured mark left by a blow to the skin is a minor injury.

clue.text: One in masculine surroundings, by and large

indicators.note: surroundings means the word for masculine is placed around the one

parts.note: manly means having masculine qualities
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A lone figure among men, for the most part.
explanation.definitionFit: Both phrases mean generally or for the most part.

clue.text: Current demand for applause

parts.note: AC is alternating current
a claim is a demand for something owed

explanation.surface: A topical demand to be cheered.
explanation.definitionFit: Public praise and enthusiastic approval is a kind of applause.

clue.text: One cut oil transport delivery

indicators.note: to transport something is to move it about, so these letters are carried into a new order

explanation.surface: A severed oil pipeline disrupts a fuel shipment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'transport' rearranges ONE CUT OIL.
explanation.definitionFit: A speaker's delivery is the manner of speaking, which this word describes.

clue.text: Turn pine back into trees

parts.note: to spin is to turn round

indicators.note: back means the word for pine is read backwards

parts.note: to yen for something is to pine or long for it

explanation.surface: Rotate a pine tree back into a woodland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pine' is a verb here, long for: YEN, which 'back' turns to NEY.
explanation.definitionFit: A small wood or copse is a cluster of trees.

clue.text: Crossing any line in a stupid way

indicators.note: crossing means mixing as in cross-breeding, so the letters of any line are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone foolishly steps over any line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crossing' looks like a container signal, but it rearranges ANY LINE.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something foolishly or senselessly is acting in a stupid way.

clue.text: Much ado about nothing in the tempest?

definitions.text: Much ado about nothing in the tempest?

parts.words: Much ado about nothing in the tempest?
parts.note: a great fuss over a trifle, pictured as bad weather inside a teacup, with both Shakespeare comedies named as a red herring

explanation.surface: Two Shakespeare plays seem to be referenced together.
explanation.walkthrough: The capital-looking titles are Shakespeare plays, but here they are plain words: a great fuss and a storm.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes making a huge fuss over something trivial, like a gale in a tiny cup.

clue.text: Tell a story about one victory for a great-uncle, perhaps

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the story word goes around the others

parts.note: to relate is to narrate
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Someone narrates a triumph won by an elderly family member.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' marks the great-uncle as one example of the class.
explanation.definitionFit: A great-uncle is one example of a family member.

clue.text: Rude books supporting part of Oxford

indicators.note: in a down clue the supporting piece sits below the other

parts.note: an Oxford is a type of shoe, and the insole is part of it
NT is the New Testament, a set of books

explanation.surface: Impolite volumes are propping up a section of a university city.
explanation.walkthrough: Oxford is not the city but a style of lace-up shoe.
explanation.definitionFit: Insolent means disrespectful and impertinent, which is rude.

clue.text: Cold kid to reserve energy for game

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold on taps
to rib is to tease or kid
to bag something is to reserve or claim it
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A chilly child tries to save his strength for a match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'kid' and 'reserve' are verbs here, not nouns.
explanation.definitionFit: A card game scored with pegs on a board is an example of a game.

clue.text: Almost satisfy worker — that's nice

indicators.note: almost means the final letter of the word for satisfy is lost

parts.note: to please is to satisfy
an ant is the classic worker insect

explanation.surface: A boss nearly keeps a labourer happy, which is good.
explanation.definitionFit: Pleasant and nice are synonyms for agreeable.

clue.text: Generously provides soldiers with good beers

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, British army soldiers
ales are types of beer

explanation.surface: Troops are lavishly given decent beer.
explanation.definitionFit: To regale someone is to entertain them lavishly with food and drink.

clue.text: Canon protects two bishops from the detritus

indicators.note: protects means wrapping around, so the canon word encloses the bishops

parts.note: a canon is a rule or principle
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop, here given twice

explanation.surface: A churchman shields two bishops from the debris.
explanation.walkthrough: Canon is not a clergyman but a law.
explanation.definitionFit: Rubble is broken stone and debris, a form of detritus.

clue.text: Ladies' man has good look around single exit

indicators.note: around means the good-look pair is wrapped around the other letters

parts.note: lo is an old word meaning look
I is one, a single
to go is to exit

explanation.surface: A womaniser casts an appreciative eye around one departure door.
explanation.walkthrough: The pair G-LO is split by I-GO: G-IGO-LO.
explanation.definitionFit: A gigolo is a man paid to escort women, a kept lover.

clue.text: The army's moral failing on smear, oddly

indicators.note: in an across clue one piece placed on another follows it
oddly means take the first, third and fifth letters of smear

parts.note: a vice is a moral failing

explanation.surface: The army's lapse in morals is a strange slur.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The army's' reads as possessive; the 's is 'is', linking definition to wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: The armed forces are known as the services, and the army is one of them.

clue.text: Sleep that's welcome on board ship — show gratitude

indicators.note: on board means inside the ship letters

parts.note: SS is steamship
ie is id est, Latin for that is
ta is a British informal thank-you

explanation.surface: A nap is gratefully received aboard a vessel, with thanks.
explanation.walkthrough: TA is everyday British slang for thank you.
explanation.definitionFit: An afternoon nap in hot countries is a kind of sleep.

clue.text: Spheres of knowledge concerning charitable donations

parts.note: re means about or concerning
alms are gifts to the poor

explanation.surface: Learned fields relating to giving to charity.
explanation.definitionFit: Realms are domains or fields, such as areas of study.

clue.text: A table leg gets broken — it's of no importance!

indicators.note: a broken item comes apart, so these letters are reassembled in a new order

explanation.surface: A piece of furniture is damaged, but it does not matter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gets broken' rearranges A TABLE LEG; the definition describes a thing, 'it'.
explanation.definitionFit: A trifle or triviality is something unimportant.

clue.text: Some result — a natural leader's wife!

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A natural outcome, someone says, for the wife of a ruler.
explanation.definitionFit: The wife of a Muslim ruler bears the feminine form of his title.

clue.text: Almost always covering fine for call up

indicators.note: covering means the shortened always goes around the fine
almost means the last letter of the word for always is removed

parts.note: ever means always
OK means fine

explanation.surface: Someone is nearly always paying a penalty for being summoned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Almost' cuts EVER to EVE, which then encloses OK.
explanation.definitionFit: To evoke a memory is to summon or bring it to mind.

clue.text: Short-lived violent demonstration dropped mood

indicators.note: violent means the letters are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: A brief, aggressive protest lost its spirit.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove the letters of MOOD from DEMONSTRATION ('dropped'), and 'violent' rearranges what remains.
explanation.definitionFit: Transient means lasting only briefly, fleeting.
